Criteria.TestCondition: All functionality can be accessed and executed using only the keyboard.
Criteria.TesterComment: Some things on this page work with a mouse but not with the keyboard, so keyboard users cannot use them. "Search Stories" works with a mouse but can't be reached with the keyboard, and nothing else on the page does the same thing (Search Stories is a header item. No reached stop is a stories link or does that job. The search box and SEARCH button search the 'All' scope, not stories.). If you disagree, tell your assistant. We looked for: things a mouse can click that the keyboard never reaches, including inside frames; menus that open when the mouse rests on them; custom controls that ignore Enter and Space; and tooltips with information found nowhere else. Results are for the browser used (version 153.0.8010.12).

Criteria.TestCondition: Individual keystrokes do not require specific timings for activation of functionality.

Criteria.TestCondition: There is no keyboard trap.
Criteria.TesterComment: We could not finish this test, so a person needs to check it. Tabbing from an error state (after pressing the button in form1) did not finish (navigation). The page seems to load more content as you scroll, and the recording could not show all of it; content after the feed was reached only by Shift+Tab from the end.

Criteria.TestCondition: A visible indication of focus is provided when focus is on the interface component.
DisabilityImpact: With Limited Language, Cognitive, and Learning Abilities
Criteria.TesterComment: Some elements don't show when they have keyboard focus, so keyboard users can lose track of where they are. When "SDE SDE" (button) gets focus, nothing on or around it changes that we could see, so keyboard users can't tell focus is there. To see it, load the page and press Tab 2 times. If you can see a focus indicator we missed, tell your assistant. We could not get a clear before-and-after view of "Help and Support" (button) (its focus style draws an outline or a shadow that our pictures did not show where it is), so a person needs to check whether it shows focus: load the page and press Tab 3 times. 7 other element(s) showed focus clearly.

Criteria.TestCondition: When an interface component receives focus, it does not initiate an unexpected change of context.
DisabilityImpact: With Limited Language, Cognitive, and Learning Abilities
Criteria.TesterComment: We could not finish this test, so a person needs to check it. The page has menus or sections that open to show more controls, and the Tab key did not reach every control inside some of them ("All All"), so a person needs to check what they hold.

Criteria.TestCondition: The focus order preserves the meaning and operability of the web page.
DisabilityImpact: With Limited Language, Cognitive, and Learning Abilities
Criteria.TesterComment: Keyboard focus moves through parts of the page in an order that doesn't make sense, which can confuse keyboard and screen reader users. The focus order doesn't make sense here: after opening "All All" (button), the next Tab does not go into what it revealed. After opening the All dropdown, the next Tab skips its five options and goes to the search box, so the revealed content is not reached after its trigger.. If you disagree, tell your assistant. Focus follows the page's reading order, forward and backward.
